extracted.subtask_description: An index/listing of COPE (Committee on Publication Ethics) guideline documents covering publication ethics topics such as peer review, authorship, retractions, editorial board duties, conflicts of interest, text recycling, and institutional cooperation. The page is intended to point editors, publishers and researchers to formal guidance on expected ethical practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing peer reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The COPE guidelines Editing peer reviews, are intended to advise editors, publishers, and researchers on expected practices and appropriate circumstances regarding the editing of peer reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidelines look at the need for journals to amend peer reviews, and provide insight into situations where this might be an appropriate course of action. Journals should have clear policies on…

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial board participation
rubrics_metrics.description: These COPE Guidelines provide an overview of editorial board appointment and engagement, roles and responsibilities, and key details to consider during recruitment such as participation on multiple editorial boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COPE Guidelines are formal COPE policy and are intended to advise editors and publishers on expected publication ethics practice. Key points Editorial ro…

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest / Competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts of interest / Competing interests (listed as a topic/category related to journal management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a core topic area within journal management and linked guideline pages; intended to guide editors on identification and handling of competing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for managing the relationships between society owned journals, their society, and publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals of ‘Learned Societies’ and ‘Professional Associations’ are an important part of the scientific literature. Regardless of the publication arrangements (ie, self-published by the society, published under contract with a professional publishing house, or some combination of both) and the number of journals affiliated with that society, the policies of and the relationships among the j…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Journal management. Guidance addresses governance, policy clarity, and ethical considerations for relationships between societies and publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Transparency and Best Practice in Scholarly Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction The Committee on Publication Ethics (COPE), the Directory of Open Access Journals (DOAJ), the Open Access Scholarly Publishers Association (OASPA), and the World Association of Medical Editors (WAME) are scholarly o…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers ethical oversight and journal management principles intended to set standards for transparent and best-practice publishing across stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals’ Best Practices for ensuring consent for publishing medical case reports: guidance from COPE
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication of case reports is a common practice in medical journals, and increasingly in basic science journals when an article illustrates a specific scientific point (e.g., a genetic phenotype). There is no doubt that case reports are valuable in the academic literature. However, they pose a specific ethical challenge for journals because, by their ve…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Ethical oversight; Intellectual property. Guidance focuses on consent processes and protections required when publishing identifiable or sensitive case material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of information among editors-in-chief regarding possible misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: This guidance has been drafted following a COPE Discussion Forum in 2013, and Discussion Document in 2014 on the subject, and it was initiated in the wake of a number of high-profile cases of research misconduct in which the sharing of information between the relevant editors-in-chief (EiCs) was crucial to the final settlement of the cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background: Sharing of information among EiCs is discussed in relation to allegations of misconduct, complaints and appeals, conflicts of interest, and ethical oversight. Provides practical points on when and how editors might communicate about potential misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text recycling guidelines for editors
rubrics_metrics.description: A common issue encountered by editors is overlap of text with an author’s own previously published work, particularly with the increasing use of plagiarism detection software. This practice is known as ‘text recycling’ (also sometimes referred to as ‘self-plagiarism’). Opinions on the acceptability of text recycling vary greatly and it can be a challenge for editors to know how to deal with it…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Intellectual property. Guidance helps editors distinguish acceptable reuse from problematic self-plagiarism and outlines possible editorial responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for Editors: research, audit and service evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations regarding what type of study requires ethical approval vary worldwide. In some countries all studies require ethical approval but in others not. This may lead to submission to journals of manuscripts relating to such studies that do not satisfy the journal’s normal requirement for independent ethical approval, and rejection of the manuscript because of misunderstanding of local regu…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Journal management. Advises editors on handling submissions that are research, audit or service evaluations and how to assess whether ethical approval is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines for the Board of Directors of Learned Society Journals
rubrics_metrics.description: The journals of Learned Societies are an important part of the scientific literature. Their management should be of the highest quality and ethically sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises directors of Learned Societies on governance, ethical obligations, and maintaining high editorial standards despite economic and political realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to handle authorship disputes: a guide for new researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the main tasks of COPE’s education committee is to reduce unethical behaviour. This involves the rather bold step of defining when people have been behaving unethically, and then providing suggestions on how they can avoid doing so in the future. To this end we have written, and tested on a group of authors, a guide for young researchers on the area of authorship, which many people agree…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Authorship and contributorship. Aimed at new researchers to clarifying unethical practices and offering advice on preventing and resolving authorship disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines for peer reviewers (English)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review in all its forms plays an important role in ensuring the integrity of the scholarly record. The process depends to a large extent on trust, and requires that everyone involved behaves responsibly and ethically. Peer reviewers play a central and critical part in the peer-review process, but too often come to the role without any guidance and unaware of their ethical obligations. COPE…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Peer review processes. Provides reviewers with expectations about ethical behaviour, responsibilities in evaluating manuscripts, and awareness of obligations (confidentiality, conflicts, integrity).

rubrics_metrics.name: A short guide to ethical editing for new editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Background/structure Becoming an editor of a journal is an exciting but daunting task, especially if you are working alone without day to day contact with editorial colleagues. This short guide aims to summarise key issues and to provide links to relevant pages of the COPE website as well as those of other organisations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Ethical oversight; Journal management. Summarises key ethical issues for new editors and points to further COPE resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation between research institutions and journals on research integrity cases: guidance COPE
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary Institutions and journals both have important duties relating to research and publication misconduct. Institutions are responsible for the conduct of their researchers and for encouraging a healthy research environment. Journals are responsible for the conduct of their editors, for safeguarding the research record, and for ensuring the reliability of everything t…
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category: Ethical oversight. Guidance describes roles and interactions between institutions and journals when addressing research integrity cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: …COPE's Retraction guidelines for advice and guidance for editors: when should a retraction be considered, what to include in a notice, how quickly to issue a retraction, who should issue a retraction, and what to do when there is inconclusive evidence of a retraction.
